sections.h2: What the Ocean County Clerk does for a seller
sections.html:
Your deed ends up with the Ocean County Clerk, a constitutional officer who oversees the filing and recording of every paper that touches ownership or transfer of real estate in the county. Passports and county elections run through the same office, so expect a busy counter.

For a seller, the moment of recording is when the land record changes hands. The state's transfer fee is collected at that point too. Mail or bring the deed with every required form attached, because a package missing a page or an affidavit can come back unrecorded and push your closing date out.

The main office sits in the courthouse at 118 Washington Street in Toms River, and three more service points cover other parts of the county.

sections.h2: What does a deed need before the clerk will record it?
sections.html:
First, it has to go to the clerk for the county where the land actually sits, with the transfer fee paperwork attached. A deed filed in the wrong county must be recorded over again in the right one, the State fee comes back on Form RTF-3, and the county portion is reclaimed from the wrong county's recording office.

  • State the full consideration on the deed, since the realty transfer fee is figured on that amount.
  • Attach Form RTF-1, the Affidavit of Consideration for Use by Seller, to any deed claiming a full or partial exemption.
  • For a house with new construction, print NEW CONSTRUCTION at the top of the first page and add an affidavit.
  • A deed over $1,000,000 also carries Form RTF-1EE for the percent fee.

County recording charges are added to the state fee, and the clerk sets that schedule. Phone the office for the current amount before you send anything.

sections.h2: How much transfer fee will an Ocean County seller owe?
sections.html:
The fee works in price brackets, counted per $500. Where the price is $350,000 or lower, the first $150,000 costs $2.00 per $500, the stretch from $150,000 to $200,000 costs $3.35, and anything beyond that costs $3.90. A price above $350,000 uses a separate schedule that opens at $2.90 per $500 and climbs to $4.80 in the band from $200,000 to $550,000.

A typical owned home in the county is valued at $398,400, so a typical sale lands on the higher schedule. Several deeds owe nothing at all: a parent-to-child deed, a deed from an executor to an heir, and a deed recorded within 90 days after a divorce decree. Qualifying seniors and blind or disabled sellers pay a reduced partial rate. Your closing attorney or title company works out which column fits your sale.

Toms River is the county seat, and 33 municipalities make up the county. Mid-2025 population is estimated at 673,746, and Lakewood Township has the most people of any town. Owners live in 80.7 percent of the 243,843 households counted for 2020 to 2024. Typical household income is $89,863 and typical gross rent is $1,755.

With four of every five households owning, the typical seller is leaving a home lived in for years. The town where the house sits decides which tax collector you phone and which school district serves it, yet one county clerk records the deed for all 33 towns.

The Garden State Parkway has fed commuter growth since 1954, and NJ Transit buses connect Lakewood and Toms River with New York and Newark. If the house is near a bus stop, say so in the listing, since buyers ask about commutes.

sections.h2: What should a seller ask the clerk before closing?
sections.html:
Find out what is already on record against the property. Liens appear in the land records, and a tax sale certificate recorded there must be paid off at closing. Whoever holds such a certificate has to record it in the county clerk's deed room within 90 days of the sale, which is how an unpaid-tax lien can surface.

  • Order a property search for open mortgages, judgments and certificates under your name and the names of earlier owners.
  • Confirm which office takes your deed, the Toms River courthouse or a branch, and check that day's hours.
  • If the house came through an estate, ask your attorney which exemption belongs on the deed.
  • Ask whether an earlier deed went to the wrong county, since that can require a refund filing.

After filing, request a recorded copy so you hold proof that the transfer happened.

sections.h2: From signed contract to recorded deed
sections.html:
Once both sides sign, the title company or attorney searches the land records and prepares the deed with the full price stated. You sign, the transfer fee forms are clipped on, and the packet goes to the clerk for the county where the land lies. When the clerk accepts it, the record changes and the fee is collected.

Selling to a cash buyer as-is leaves this sequence alone. Recording still happens in the same county, on the same forms, with the same fee deducted from your side of the settlement sheet. What disappears is the repair list and the lender's timeline, which often makes recording the last open item before funds move.

faqs.q: Which office records a deed in Ocean County?
faqs.a: The Ocean County Clerk records deeds and other papers that affect ownership. Its courthouse office at 118 Washington Street in Toms River can be reached at (732) 929-2018.

faqs.q: Who pays the realty transfer fee on an Ocean County sale?
faqs.a: The seller. It is a charge on the seller for recording the deed.

faqs.q: Can I record my deed in a different county by mistake and fix it?
faqs.a: Yes. Record it again in the county where the land lies, file Form RTF-3 to get the State's share refunded, and ask the wrong county's recording office to return the county share.

faqs.q: Does an estate sale owe the transfer fee?
faqs.a: Not when an executor or administrator deeds the house to an heir or devisee named under the will or intestacy laws. If the executor sells to anyone else, the deed is not exempt.

faqs.q: How many Ocean County homes are owner-occupied?
faqs.a: About 80.7 percent for 2020 to 2024, across 243,843 households. The middle value of an owned home is $398,400.
